top_stories.title: Anthropic's Record-Breaking IPO
points: AI company Anthropic (maker of the Claude chatbot) began trading on Nasdaq under ticker ANT, in the largest tech IPO on record.

Reported pricing and raise figures varied widely by outlet: CNBC cited $98/share raising $81.2B (~$980B valuation); Seeking Alpha cited $83/share raising $81.3B plus a $26B private placement for a $107.3B total deal (~$1.5T fully diluted valuation); Opening Bell cited $83/share raising ~$68.5B (~$1.08T valuation); Bloomberg cited a $107.3B combined public/private raise surpassing SpaceX's prior record.
The deal surpasses previous record IPOs (variously cited as Saudi Aramco's 2019 listing or SpaceX's private raise five months earlier).

Revenue is growing extremely fast (10x year-over-year to ~$16.3B per Seeking Alpha, or $17B per Opening Bell, roughly 12x prior year) but the company posted a massive net loss (~$80.7B per Seeking Alpha, ~$104B per Opening Bell), driven mainly by non-cash valuation/convertible-note charges rather than operating losses.
News of the IPO lifted Nasdaq futures (+2.1%) and broader tech and S&P 500 futures (+1.2%), reflecting investor enthusiasm for AI infrastructure plays.

The listing intensifies competition with OpenAI, Google, Meta, and Microsoft in the AI race, and Anthropic will be added to broad tech indices and potentially the S&P 500, giving institutional investors direct access.

unique_angles.point: Analysts flagged that Anthropic has $900.9B in compute (computing power/data center) commitments against only $35.3B trailing revenue—a fixed cost that doesn't shrink if sales disappoint.
The IPO is framed as Wall Street's largest-ever bet on 'artificial superintelligence' (AI systems that could exceed human capability across all domains).
Coverage focused on testing investor appetite for pure-play AI stocks amid broader market skepticism, with live-blog tracking of the trading debut.
Financial advisors specifically cautioned retail investors against buying on day one, citing typical first-day volatility and pricing-discovery risk.
Early investors including Google are positioned to reap billions in returns from the listing.

top_stories.title: Nvidia Leadership Turmoil Overshadows Strong Earnings
points: Nvidia reported strong financial results (per Opening Bell, sales topped estimates by 6.3%, the biggest beat in 8 quarters) but shares fell/remained down over 20% in 2026 as investors reacted to leadership uncertainty.
CEO Jensen Huang's departure left a leadership vacuum; new CEO Colette Kress and Chair Harvey Jones failed to reassure investors in their first earnings presentation.
Kress canceled progress on Huang's China business plans to avoid optics problems, a move described as defensible but unsettling to markets.
An Uber co-founder urged Nvidia employees to stage a walkout demanding Huang's return, highlighting executive-stability concerns at a company critical to AI chip supply.

unique_angles.point: Described Nvidia as in 'crisis mode' due to the leadership vacuum in the chip supply chain.
Cited the specific earnings beat figure (sales topped estimates by 6.3%, best in 8 quarters).
Provided the most detail on the Kress/China decision and framed it as defensible policy versus market perception.

top_stories.title: Strong Retail Earnings Lift Target, Lowe's, TJX
points: Target posted $27.1 billion in quarterly sales (+7.1%), beat earnings with $2.65 EPS (including a $0.50 tariff-refund benefit), raised its full-year outlook, and saw comparable sales growth of 5.6%.
Target also reported a 5% jump in foot traffic, its largest gain since January 2022, attributed to a strategy of refreshing inventory late into December for last-minute holiday shoppers.
Lowe's comparable sales rose 1.8% to $22.76 billion quarterly; the company raised full-year guidance to ~$92.5 billion after prior weakness.
TJX (T.J. Maxx parent) reported comparable sales up 4% in Q3, revenue of $15.85 billion (topping estimates), raised full-year earnings guidance, and saw its stock jump 9%.
TJX's CEO credited the gains to stocking fresh inventory arriving within 10 days of Christmas, exploiting a gap left by competitors who had already sold through or marked down seasonal stock.

unique_angles.point: Target's CEO Michael Fiddelke specifically credited the late-inventory-refresh strategy for the foot-traffic gain; October retail data showed consumers pulling back on big purchases like cars and furniture while sustaining other spending.
Provided consolidated hard numbers across all three retailers (Target, Lowe's, TJX) in one roundup alongside broader market context.

top_stories.title: Federal Reserve December Rate Decision Uncertainty
points: Fed officials are split on the size of a potential December rate move, with debate over whether to hike by the standard 25 basis points or a larger 50 basis point increase (a larger-than-normal rate hike).
New York Fed President John Williams ruled out a 50 bp hike, while Governor Chris Waller argued for one, saying skipping it now would force the Fed to hike again in January.
Minutes show almost all Fed officials judged further rate hikes would likely be appropriate; markets are fully pricing in a December hike, per Seeking Alpha, eliminating pause expectations.

unique_angles.point: Explained Waller's reasoning via 'forward guidance' (clear Fed communication about future policy plans) and noted Fed Chair Warsh has historically resisted forward guidance, creating a policy dilemma.
Stated markets have fully priced in a December hike, removing any expectation of a pause.

items.title: GTA VI Launch and Take-Two Economics
points: Grand Theft Auto VI launched the same day as the Anthropic IPO, with 17.1 million units pre-sold as of Wednesday.

Wells Fargo raised its full-year unit forecast to 65 million, while Take-Two's own guidance is for $8-8.2 billion in net bookings (total revenue from game and in-game sales) for fiscal 2027—well below Wells Fargo's $9.76 billion estimate.
The game is priced at $79; Take-Two's parent stock fell double-digits year-to-date after an 18% prior-year drop in net bookings to $1.6 billion in Q2.
The dual Anthropic/GTA VI launches created a rare real-time comparison between investor appetite for AI infrastructure and consumer demand for premium gaming.

items.title: Dow's Third Straight 1%+ Drop

items.title: Xi Hosts Trump and Putin for Trilateral Talks
points: Xi Jinping convened an unprecedented trilateral meeting with Trump and Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, warning that major-power rivalry breeds global instability.
The three leaders held 90-minute talks focused on preventing nuclear conflict and resolving disputes including Ukraine and Iran.

items.title: China's AI-Driven Jobs Squeeze
points: Bloomberg analysis found double-digit percentage declines in hiring for roles most exposed to AI disruption and automation in China.
Graduates and displaced workers are rushing to acquire new AI skills to stay competitive in a tightening labor market.

items.title: Musk Regrets Political Spending
points: Elon Musk said he feels 'pretty foolish' about spending more than $445 million backing Republican candidates in the 2024 election cycle.
The spending drew voter backlash and was used by victorious Democrats, including newly elected Texas Senator James Talarico.

items.title: Venezuela Oil Deal Scrutiny
points: Venezuela's opposition leader is scrutinizing a $100 billion US oil deal with businessman Alejandro Betancourt involving 17 oil fields.

issues.subject: Morning Brief: All eyes on Anthropic's public market debut

headlines: Anthropic begins trading on Nasdaq under ticker ANT, testing investor appetite for pure-play AI companies amid broader market skepticism.

Fed officials split on December rate strategy: John Williams rules out a 50 basis point hike (a larger-than-normal interest rate increase), while Chris Waller argues for one to signal commitment to fighting inflation.
Target reports 5% jump in foot traffic, its largest gain since January 2022, as consumers prioritize deals and value amid inflation pressures.
TJ Maxx owner TJX surges 9% after reporting strong earnings, capitalizing on late holiday shoppers seeking fresh inventory that competitors have already depleted.
Nvidia stock tumbles despite excellent financial results, as new leadership under CEO Colette Kress fails to inspire confidence in the company's post-Jensen Huang direction.

sections.title: Nvidia's Earnings Fail to Reverse Stock Decline
points: 1. Despite strong financial performance, Nvidia shares have fallen over 20% in 2026 as investors lose confidence in the company's new leadership structure.
2. CEO Colette Kress and Chair Harvey Jones' earnings presentation on Wednesday failed to address major investor concerns about the company's future under new management.

3. CEO Jensen Huang's departure and Kress's cancellation of his China business progress—a move made to avoid optics problems—has further unsettled the market despite being a defensible policy decision.

sections.title: Fed December Meeting Shaped by Leadership Disagreement
points: 1. New York Fed President John Williams ruled out a 50 basis point hike (larger-than-normal rate increase) in December, while Governor Chris Waller countered that skipping it now means the Fed must hike again in January.

2. Waller's argument centers on market signaling: two 25 basis point increases feel less impactful than one 50 basis point increase unless the Fed explicitly promises future moves via 'forward guidance' (clear statements about future policy intentions).

3. Fed Chair Warsh has historically resisted forward guidance, potentially forcing him to choose between signaling January hikes or accepting a larger December increase—a clash of competing philosophies about effective monetary policy.

sections.title: Consumer Spending Remains Resilient Despite Inflation
points: 1. Target's 5% foot traffic increase—the strongest year-over-year gain since early 2022—reflects consumer appetite for value-priced quality goods in an inflationary environment.

2. CEO Michael Fiddelke attributed success to Target's strategy of updating inventory late into December, offering fresh products when competitors' shelves are picked over, particularly important for last-minute holiday shoppers.

3. October retail sales data showed consumers pulling back on big purchases like cars and furniture but sustaining spending in other categories, illustrating how inflation steers spending patterns rather than eliminating overall demand.

sections.title: TJ Maxx Parent Company TJX Capitalizes on Holiday Shopping Trends
points: 1. TJX shares jumped 9% after reporting strong quarterly results and raising full-year guidance, driven by investor confidence in holiday demand for discount retail.

2. CEO Ernie Herrman highlighted the company's competitive advantage: maintaining fresh inventory that arrives within 10 days of Christmas, while most traditional retailers have sold through or clearanced seasonal stock.
3. This strategy targets a specific consumer pain point—the last-minute shopper who wants immediate gratification without online delivery delays or picked-over local shelves.
